issues.competing_evidence: RXTE shock model Rana+05: 1.21±0.10 Msun; eclipse geometry Mukai+03: <0.67 Msun; NuSTAR Shaw+20: 0.76(+0.09/−0.08); Swift+NuSTAR Wang+21: 0.85±0.07; Wang Table 4 also reports Ramsay (2000) 0.98 with 90% interval 0.78–1.19. These methods/models are not interchangeable.
issues.why_it_matters: WD mass changes interpretation of the system and population comparisons; estimates span incompatible spectral and eclipse-model branches.
issues.needed_action: Keep all results with methods and confidence conventions. If a single community-facing preferred value is required, choose only after checking the original Ramsay article and resolving model systematics; do not average.

issues.parameter: WD effective temperature / HST UV component
issues.competing_evidence: Schmidt & Stockman+01 fit a ~35,000 K blackbody or 25,000–30,000 K atmosphere to dereddened UV-optical flux; their variable eclipse spectra also support stream/other emission, and later Mukai+03 finds a donor-caused X-ray eclipse. Rana+05 kTbb=88±2 eV and Wang+21 ~50 eV are soft X-ray accretion components, not photospheric temperatures.
issues.why_it_matters: Treating the UV or X-ray hot component as a secure WD Teff biases cooling-age and WD-temperature comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Keep the HST blackbody and atmosphere branches as candidate hot-component fits. Decide whether a white-dwarf photospheric Teff is publishable only after reviewing the original HST component decomposition and extinction assumptions.

issues.competing_evidence: Rana+05 tentatively infers 28–35 MG by assigning a circular-polarization peak to the 6th–8th cyclotron harmonic; no cyclotron spectrum and poor optical polarization data. Ferrario+15 lists ~30 MG as a secondary compilation. Barrett+20 gives 3563±730 G only under fundamental ECM from a donor corona.
issues.why_it_matters: A kG radio-plasma field and an MG accretion-region/WD field are different physical quantities; mixing them would corrupt WD-field comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Keep the 28–35 MG value explicitly tentative and region-specific, keep 3.56 kG as conditional donor-corona radio field, and do not quote a secure global WD surface field without direct cyclotron/Zeeman evidence.

issues.competing_evidence: Boyd+14 reports quadratic eclipse ephemeris dPorb/dt/P=−1.38(29)×10^-11 yr yr^-1 using a 15-year, multi-source timing compilation. Littlefield+15 finds no evidence for derivative in its 28-month eclipse set but explicitly says the result does not contradict Boyd’s longer dataset.
issues.why_it_matters: A changing orbital period affects long-term timing and could be confused with the WD spin derivative or beat evolution.
issues.needed_action: For any adopted orbital Pdot, harmonize eclipse-time datasets, time standards and error reweighting; otherwise retain the long-baseline claim and the shorter-baseline nondetection separately.

issues.competing_evidence: Staubert+03 combined and optical-only fits give different Pdot_spin values; Mukai+03 and Boyd+14 use different baselines/models; Littlefield+15 cubic polynomial and exponential spin ephemerides both fit. Published beat periods range ~49.6 d (1992) to ~61.7 d (2013), so the inherited single 49.8955 d is epoch-specific at best.
issues.why_it_matters: Beat phase controls accretion geometry and timing residuals; one fixed period can misphase observations across years.
issues.needed_action: Keep fit-specific ephemerides, epochs and models in the measurement table. Do not select one extrapolation as a measured current period without a common timing refit.

issues.competing_evidence: Rana+05 Table 4 reports 1–10 keV average 2.13×10^-11 and says fluxes correct local absorbers only while setting interstellar NH=0; nearby prose calls hard flux unabsorbed. Ridder+23 Table 3 gives 2.1×10^-11 (1–10 keV) and 4.1×10^-11 (0.1–10 keV) without a source-specific conversion input or error.
issues.why_it_matters: An ambiguous absorption correction or noncontemporaneous catalog flux can bias radio/X-ray luminosity and accretion-state comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Inspect the exact Rana Table 4 note/model and match Ridder’s V1432 row to its 4XMM detection/model/NH. Until then retain separate flux rows without calling either Ridder value unabsorbed.

issues.parameter: radio detection significance and emission site
issues.competing_evidence: Barrett+20 lists a detection with custom S/N=9.3, but Table 1 Stokes I=15±5 μJy (~3σ) and CP=+100±47% (~2.1σ). The source is unresolved; a donor-coronal fundamental ECM origin is proposed, not localized.
issues.why_it_matters: Detection thresholds affect sample membership, and the emission site determines whether the conditional kG field can be compared to WD fields.
issues.needed_action: Preserve Barrett’s published detection plus raw Stokes measurements. For thresholded population work, apply a consistent Stokes-I threshold; do not treat the donor-corona mechanism as confirmed.

issues.competing_evidence: Schmidt & Stockman+01 say an M4 V donor was detected in I band and cite Patterson+95; the original Patterson full text was not retrieved. Mukai+03 uses M2=0.31 or 0.22 Msun as assumptions; Wang+21 M2=0.22±0.02 is a CV donor-sequence/Roche-lobe estimate, not a dynamical mass. No donor Teff or secure q is found.
issues.why_it_matters: Donor mass and subtype inform evolutionary and orbital-period comparisons, but a model value may be mistaken for measurement.
issues.needed_action: Retrieve/check Patterson+95 original I-band spectrum and retain model masses separately from direct donor quantities; seek dynamical velocities or resolved donor spectrum before adopting q/Teff.

issues.competing_evidence: Boyd+14 presents a pre-record nova as the origin of asynchronism and projects synchronization near 2100. Wang+21 argues the low inferred Mdot contradicts a recent-nova classification under the short synchronization-timescale picture; its rate and timing extrapolation are also model-dependent.
issues.why_it_matters: A speculative post-nova history could be mistaken for an established evolutionary pathway connecting populations.
issues.needed_action: Keep both as hypotheses, label model assumptions, and do not use the proposed nova/resynchronization scenario as an established sequence or catalog classification.

issues.parameter: legacy distance input and dependent luminosities
issues.competing_evidence: Historical ~230 pc distance is quoted by Schmidt & Stockman+01 from Watson+95 and used in older Rana+05 luminosities/accretion-rate estimates; HST discussion adjusts it to ~200 pc for assumed I-band extinction. Current Gaia EDR3/Bailer-Jones geometric posterior is 449.66 pc. Original Watson distance method/error has not been independently checked.
issues.why_it_matters: Reusing old distance-dependent luminosities or Mdot alongside the Gaia distance without rescaling mixes incompatible assumptions.
issues.needed_action: If historical luminosities or the Rana Mdot are quantitatively reused, retrieve Watson+95 and decide whether to recompute explicitly from the newer posterior. Keep old published inputs distinct meanwhile.
